I4.quote: Although this wood based carbon generally has a surface area only around 700 m²/g with a relatively low mesopore volume, it was utilized because it has a surface area approximately 70 times larger than the VGCF [10].

notes: I4 not met. The only surface-area statements in the paper are the quoted sentence on Norit Darco G-60. The 700 m²/g is stated as what this kind of carbon 'generally has', which protocol §15 Amendment 1 excludes; it is not given as a value measured on, or supplied for, the sample used. The '70 times larger than the VGCF [10]' clause is a ratio attributed to earlier work and gives no area value for any measured sample. No BET, Langmuir or other surface-area measurement is reported for any sample in the text, Table 1 or any figure (all page images checked). Input contains the main article only; no supplementary file was provided. I1: uptake measured volumetrically (Sieverts-type gas reaction controller, Section 2.2.2, and a manual high-pressure system, Section 2.2.1) on the carbons at 23°C; most PCI values are described as 'not significantly above the background' and the manual-system VGCF values are upper limits (<0.7, <0.5, <0.2 wt.%), but these are original gas-phase measurements. Table 1 symbols (±, <, 23°C) were read from the page image because the text layer renders them as '6', ',' and '8C'. Earlier exclusion codes do not apply: experimental, gas-phase, carbon sorbents, primary research article, no retraction notice in the text, and T and P are stated for Table 1 values.
